description: Provenance-labelled parametric design knowledge — type pairings, OKLCH palette recipes, themes, macrostructures, and component cookbooks — loaded advisory-style during a build. Craft references are knowledge, not rules: they never participate in the six-family rule-selection contract.

observed.statement: The maintainer has applied each recipe below in shipped interfaces and reviewed artifacts: the pairing grammar, OKLCH recipe formulas, theme registers, macrostructure anatomies, and cookbook items recur across the author's own frontend work.
The working example assets in domains/frontend/examples/ demonstrate the macrostructure anatomies (hero placement, divider treatment, button voice, image treatment) as rendered plates.

inferred.statement: Palette recipes are expressed as OKLCH lightness/chroma ranges rather than exact hues, so one recipe yields distinct palettes for different products without repeating the same color identity.
Each macrostructure lists the theme axes and treatment axes it interacts with, so the direction step can pick one explicitly and state it out loud.

Each theme fixes one complete identity and maps onto the three declared theme axes (paperBand, displayStyle, accentHue), so a theme pick slots into the direction's declared identity without a parallel vocabulary.

assumed.statement: The consuming design skill has browser evidence or rendered screenshots available for material work; craft references sharpen decisions but never replace observed evidence.

unknown.statement: Whether a future craft item should graduate into a bundled design rule is decided only through the tiered promotion bar with full human-reviewed evidence, never by the craft corpus itself.
The theme catalog is not a closed contract: themes may be added or replaced as shipped work accumulates, and the identity-fingerprint mechanism, not the catalog, enforces diversification.
